correctness.rationale: Conditional finite-permutation counting proves each branch of the joint probability table for all n≥3; subtracting Bernoulli means yields the six-case matrix and summing gives fg/[(n-1)(n-2)]. Independence follows by equality of conditional and marginal Bernoulli probabilities; aggregate non-independence follows from identity versus a noncommuting permutation. Exhaustive exact rational finite verification supplies 3,773 cross-covariance and aggregate checks but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The complete six-branch second-order dependence profile quantifies how a deterministic permutation test influences commutator agreements versus original fixed points. Its covariance f(n-f)/[(n-1)(n-2)] is invariant under changing all nontrivial cycle lengths; the degenerate all-pairs-independence phase for every derangement is striking because aggregate counts remain dependent. This is a universal structural classification motivated by commutator randomization diagnostics, not an arbitrary special case or a marginal Poisson restatement.
